prompt.context: Our client is Great Burger (GB), the fourth largest fast food chain worldwide by number of stores. GB competes head-to-head with McDonald's, Wendy's, Burger King, and KFC, offering food and combos for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. GB operates under a franchising model with 85% of its stores owned by franchisees who pay a franchise fee; major business decisions (menu, store look) are controlled by GB. As part of its growth strategy, GB has analyzed potential acquisition targets including Heavenly Donuts (HD), a growing doughnut producer with both US and international store presence. HD also operates under a franchising model, but franchises areas/regions rather than individual restaurants — the area franchisee is required to open a certain number of stores. GB's CEO has hired McKinsey to advise on whether GB should acquire HD.
prompt.question: Should GB acquire Heavenly Donuts?

clarifying_info.q: What is HD's current market share in the US?
clarifying_info.a: HD has US sales of $700M. US doughnut market is $10/capita x 300M people = $3B, implying ~23% share (round to 25% for calculations).

clarifying_info.q: Does GB have prior M&A or integration experience?
clarifying_info.a: That is one of the areas worth exploring — the interviewer will not confirm either way; the candidate should surface it as a key question.

clarifying_info.q: What is the cannibalization rate if doughnuts are sold in GB stores?
clarifying_info.a: 10% of GB unit sales would be cannibalized (provided in Exhibit 2 when shown).

exhibits.title: GB and HD Store Count and Financial Summary
exhibits.shows: Side-by-side comparison of GB and HD across store geography, annual store growth rate, financial metrics (total store sales, parent company revenues, key expense line items as % of sales, profit as % of sales, sales per store, and industry average sales per store).

exhibits.title: Sales and Profitability per Store — Doughnut Cross-Sell Scenario
exhibits.shows: Per-store unit economics for GB's existing sales and for HD doughnuts sold in GB stores, plus the assumed cannibalization rate of HD products on GB products.

framework: Stand-alone value of HD: doughnut market growth, HD revenue/profit trajectory, HD growth in stores vs. same-store sales, competition, capital requirements to fund growth
Management and cultural fit: capabilities of HD top/middle management, cultural compatibility, retention risk

Synergies and strategic fit: brand compatibility, customer-base overlap, revenue synergies (cross-sell, international expansion), cost synergies (SG&A, procurement, property/equipment), GB's prior M&A integration experience
Deal execution considerations: different franchise structures (individual stores vs. area franchises), ability to manage both simultaneously, valuation and price to pay

questions.prompt: Q1: What areas would you want to explore to determine whether GB should acquire HD?
questions.guidance: A strong answer covers three main buckets: (1) Stand-alone value of HD — doughnut market growth, HD past/projected sales growth split into new stores vs. same-store sales, competitive landscape and implications for future growth, profitability/margins, and capital required to fund growth. (2) Management and cultural fit — capabilities of key management layers, cultural differences, retention risk. (3) Synergies and strategic fit — brand quality compatibility, customer-base overlap (too little suggests incompatibility, too much limits cross-marketing upside), revenue synergies, cost synergies, GB's M&A integration track record, and implications of differing franchise structures for deal execution.

questions.prompt: Q2: What potential synergies can you identify between GB and HD? (Show Exhibit 1)
questions.guidance: Cost synergies: largest opportunity is likely corporate SG&A integration; some procurement savings on shared inputs (beverages, frying oil) though ingredient overlap is limited; GB's lower property/equipment cost ratio (4.6% vs. HD's 8.5%) suggests superior lease-negotiation skills that could be leveraged for HD. Revenue synergies: sell doughnuts in GB stores or selected GB products in HD stores; GB's larger international footprint provides knowledge/skills to accelerate HD's international expansion; GB's higher sales/store vs. industry average ($1.1M vs. $0.9M) versus HD's below-average ($0.7M vs. $0.8M) suggests GB can improve HD store-location selection; GB's larger balance sheet and lower debt may provide better capital access to fund faster HD expansion.

questions.prompt: Q3: The team believes GB can double HD's US market share in 5 years and expand HD store count by 2.5x. What sales/store will HD require in 5 years? Assumptions: doughnut consumption/capita grows from $10 to $20/year; US population = 300M.
questions.guidance: Walk through the market-sizing table step by step. Current HD market share is ~23% (round to 25%). Doubling share on a doubled market yields $3B in HD sales. With 2.5x stores the required sales/store is $1.2M. A strong candidate notes this implies less than doubling same-store sales, which is reasonable given per-capita consumption is itself doubling.

math.setup: Current US market = $10 x 300M = $3B. HD current share = $700M / $3B ≈ 23% → round to 25%. US market in 5 years = $20 x 300M = $6B. HD sales in 5 years = 25% x 2 x $6B = $3B. HD stores in 5 years = 1,000 (NA stores) x 2.5 = 2,500. Required sales/store = $3B / 2,500.
steps: HD target sales in 5 years = 25% x 2 x $6B = $3B
math.answer: $1.2M sales per HD store in 5 years

questions.prompt: Q4: How would you assess the profitability impact of selling doughnuts in GB stores?
questions.guidance: A full answer covers three layers: (1) Incremental revenues — doughnuts sold per store x price, times number of GB stores; (2) Incremental costs — cost of goods, additional labor/training, software changes, marketing, distribution or in-store production investment; (3) Incremental investment — additional store space if new customers are attracted, store-layout investment for in-house production. Strong candidates also address cannibalization: doughnut sales will cannibalize GB breakfast items most heavily; estimate cannibalization using historical rates from prior GB product launches; also consider cannibalization of nearby HD stores using historical data on sales impact when a competitor doughnut outlet opens nearby.

questions.prompt: Q5: (Optional / if time permits) Using Exhibit 2, what is the incremental profit per GB store from selling 50,000 HD doughnuts/store at $2/unit at 60% margin, with a 10% cannibalization rate on GB sales?
questions.guidance: Compute HD contribution, subtract lost GB contribution from cannibalized units. If this question is skipped, tell the candidate: incremental profit per GB store = $15K (note: the casebook's stated shortcut answer; the worked math yields $5K — use the worked math for rigor).

math.setup: Incremental profit = HD contribution − cannibalized GB contribution. HD contribution = 50K units x $2 x 60%. Cannibalized GB contribution = 300K units x 10% x $3 x 50%.
steps: Cannibalized GB contribution = 300,000 x 10% x $3 x 50% = $45,000
math.answer: $15,000 incremental profit per GB store (casebook shortcut figure used; note the interviewer's own worked math gives $5K — discrepancy likely due to rounding in the shortcut)

brainstorming.prompt: What potential synergies can you think of between GB and HD?

categories.name: Cost Synergies
ideas: Integrate corporate SG&A / consolidate corporate management (largest opportunity)
Leverage combined purchasing volume on shared inputs (beverages, frying oil) to reduce food costs
Apply GB's superior lease-negotiation skills to reduce HD's property and equipment costs (HD at 8.5% vs. GB at 4.6%)

categories.name: Revenue Synergies
ideas: Sell HD doughnuts in GB stores, especially for breakfast occasion
Sell selected GB products in HD stores
Leverage GB's extensive international network to accelerate HD's global expansion beyond North America
Apply GB's superior store-location capabilities (above-industry-average sales/store) when opening new HD locations
Use GB's stronger balance-sheet access to capital to fund faster HD store rollout

recommendation: Early findings support acquiring HD — the deal can create significant value for GB
Selling HD doughnuts in GB stores could add approximately $15K in profit per GB store, implying roughly $50M in incremental annual profit across North American GB stores
Additional revenue and cost synergies (SG&A integration, procurement, international expansion, location expertise) have not yet been fully quantified but appear material
risks: Different franchise structures (individual store vs. area/regional franchising) may complicate integration and management
Cultural mismatch between the two organizations could lead to loss of key HD management talent
HD's below-industry-average sales/store and lower profit margin (4.9% vs. GB's 6.3%) suggest operational challenges that must be addressed post-acquisition
Cannibalization of GB breakfast offerings and nearby HD stores could reduce net synergy realization
Overpaying — final acquisition price must be justified by fully quantified synergies and a DCF of HD's stand-alone value
next_steps: Quantify remaining revenue and cost synergies to support final acquisition price recommendation
Model HD stand-alone DCF and determine maximum price GB should pay
Develop post-merger integration plan addressing franchise structure harmonization, cultural alignment, and management retention
Assess feasibility and timeline of selling doughnuts in GB stores (supply chain, store layout, employee training)
